title: Count Good Triplets in an Array
summary: Given two arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, both permutations of [0, 1, ..., n-1], count the number of good triplets.
statement: Given two arrays nums1 and nums2 of length n, both permutations of [0, 1, ..., n-1], count the number of good triplets. A good triplet (x, y, z) satisfies pos1x < pos1y < pos1z and pos2x < pos2y < pos2z, where pos1v and pos2v are the indices of value v in nums1 and nums2 respectively.
constraints: Both arrays are permutations of 0 through n-1.
A value triplet must appear in increasing index order in both permutations.
Return the number of such triplets; the result may exceed 32-bit range.
hints: Map nums1 into the position order imposed by nums2; the task becomes counting increasing subsequences of length three.
For each middle element, count smaller values to its left and greater values to its right with Fenwick trees.
Scan left-to-right for smaller counts, then right-to-left for greater counts; sum their products.
Every increasing triplet has a unique middle. The product chooses its valid left and right endpoints independently, counting each triplet once.
editorial: Every increasing triplet has a unique middle. The product chooses its valid left and right endpoints independently, counting each triplet once.

tests.explanation: Only values 0,1,3 preserve increasing order in both arrays, so return 1.
Exactly four value triplets have increasing positions in both permutations.
